BiblicalUsage: Reseph is named in Sennacherib's taunt, among the cities whose gods could not deliver them out of the hand of Assyria: Have the gods of the nations delivered them which my fathers have destroyed? The gods of Reseph could not deliver it, and the king of Assyria knew it before he sent his taunt.
TheologicalSignificance: What I take from this is that Reseph is named so that the taunt is answered, for the God of Hezekiah did what the gods of Reseph could not.
RelatedPeople: King Hezekiah; Sennacherib, King of Assyria; Isaiah
